It goes beyond mere facts to encompass the ability to make sense of situations, apply knowledge appropriately, and make wise decisions or judgments. Wisdom involves intuition, empathy, and an understanding of how things relate to each other and to the human condition. It is often subjective and context-dependent, as it incorporates ethical, moral, and emotional dimensions.

In essence, facts are the building blocks of knowledge, while wisdom is the skillful and practical application of that knowledge to navigate life's complexities and challenges. While facts provide the foundation, wisdom helps us interpret, contextualize, and use those facts effectively.
